identity_marker: stark white Aida cloth, round wooden hoop, bright red floss, and silver needle
continuity_anchors: brightly lit crafting table with a natural oak wood grain surface under soft, diffused overhead studio lighting
video_goal: Demonstrate how to create a basic cross-stitch on Aida cloth while maintaining even thread tension.
single_prompt: A Close-up shot focuses on the stark white Aida cloth, round wooden hoop, bright red floss, and silver needle resting in their starting positions. Hands place a square of the fabric evenly over the inner ring. The camera smoothly transitions to an Over-the-shoulder view as hands press the outer ring down over the fabric, gently tugging the edges to make it taut and twisting the top metal screw to secure it. Gliding into an Extreme close-up, fingers pinch the end of a strand of floss and push it precisely through the eye of the needle. Shifting smoothly to a First-person view, the needle tip pokes up from beneath the taut fabric, emerging cleanly through a specific bottom-left grid hole. The camera pulls back slightly into a Close-up as fingers pull the thread upward until only a 1-inch tail remains visible underneath, holding the tail flat against the back. Moving seamlessly into an Extreme close-up, the needle tip is inserted down into the grid hole diagonally up and to the right of the starting hole. The view widens gently to a Close-up as the thread is pulled down slowly until it lays perfectly flat against the grid, forming a diagonal line without puckering. Transitioning back to a First-person view, the needle emerges from the hole directly below the top-right hole, representing the bottom-right corner of the stitch square. The camera zooms into an Extreme close-up as the needle is pushed down into the top-left hole, crossing the thread directly over the first diagonal line to form an X. Pulling back to a Close-up, the thread is pulled taut to complete a perfect X shape, and a finger gently taps the stitch to demonstrate it is snug. The camera shifts to an Over-the-shoulder view as hands complete two more identical X stitches directly to the right of the first one, forming a uniform, evenly tensioned row. Finally, the camera moves into a Close-up as the hoop is flipped over to reveal the back side, and the needle is slid horizontally underneath the three vertical thread loops to secure the loose tail. The entire process takes place on a brightly lit crafting table with a natural oak wood grain surface under soft, diffused overhead studio lighting.
